title: E-Signature Tools for HubSpot: QuickSigner, DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, and HubSpot Quotes — Jon Martin
seoTitle: HubSpot E-Signature Tools: Quotes, DocuSign, Dropbox Sign
description: HubSpot quote e-sign compared with DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, and QuickSigner: plans, prices, and which ones actually connect to HubSpot. Checked Nov 23, 2026.
dek: First ask whether HubSpot's own quote e-sign already covers the job. Then pick a native CRM integration, or a cheaper tool you are willing to wire up.
Four options lined up for HubSpot teams: HubSpot quotes, DocuSign, Dropbox Sign, and QuickSigner.

sections.label: Start with HubSpot's own quote e-sign

blocks.html: Before you add a signer, check whether HubSpot already covers it. HubSpot can collect e-signatures on quotes. Per HubSpot, quote e-sign is powered by Dropbox Sign, and you don't need a Dropbox Sign account for the regular quote flow.

On the current quoting tools, e-sign on current quotes needs a Revenue Hub subscription and a Revenue Hub seat. HubSpot's own examples: 25 e-signatures per user per month on Revenue Hub Professional, pooled across the account, and 50 e-signatures per user per month on Revenue Hub Enterprise, pooled across the account. If you need more, the catalog lists $60 a month for 100 more e-signatures a month, on Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise only.

Revenue Hub seat list prices are $95 per seat per month (Revenue Seat, Professional, catalog list price) and $140 per seat per month (Revenue Seat, Enterprise, catalog list price). That is the price of the hub, not of e-sign on its own, because e-sign is a feature of the hub.

One warning for anyone reading older guides: legacy quotes are no longer available to new users. Also, legacy quote e-sign is a Sales Hub feature, and HubSpot's own help articles disagree on whether Starter includes it. So do not tell a new customer to plan around legacy quotes, and check your account before you rely on a Starter answer.
If the team signs sales quotes inside HubSpot and already has, or will buy, Revenue Hub, start with the native quote e-sign. Add a specialist when you need to sign documents that are not quotes.

items: Already have DocuSign and want envelopes from HubSpot records: DocuSign.
Want signature requests from contact, company, or deal records, saved back: Dropbox Sign.
Want the lowest published price and can own an API build: QuickSigner.

blocks.html: QuickSigner has an affiliate link and the others do not. That is not a reason to rank it ahead of the native HubSpot options. It is the cheap choice that takes developer time.
HubSpot sales and operations teams that want documents or quotes signed without leaving the CRM, or a cheaper signer than the enterprise tools.
Not for: a signer comparison with no CRM context.

DocuSign has an official HubSpot app. It works with all HubSpot products and plans, and creates, sends, and tracks envelopes from contact, company, and deal records. It needs a paid DocuSign plan and a DocuSign Admin, plus a HubSpot Super Admin or App Marketplace permission to connect.

Note that custom property mapping needs DocuSign eSignature Business Pro or higher. And it fills envelopes with HubSpot property values but is not a full data sync app, so treat it as envelope creation from the record, not a two-way data sync.

Prices from DocuSign's pricing page: Personal: $11 a month on an annual plan ($132 a year), with 5 envelopes a month; Standard: $30 per user per month on an annual plan ($360 a year); Business Pro: $45 per user per month on an annual plan ($540 a year). Standard and Business Pro: 100 envelopes per user per year on annual plans, or 10 per user per month on monthly plans.

Dropbox Sign has an official HubSpot app as well. It sends signature requests from Contact, Company, or Deal records in HubSpot, and the signed file saves back to the record. Note that requests sent from hellosign.com aren't tracked in HubSpot, so send from inside the integration.
HubSpot's own quote e-sign is powered by the same engine, but that is a different thing from installing the Dropbox Sign app for general documents.

Prices from the Dropbox Sign pricing page: Essentials: $15 a month for 1 user; Standard: $25 per user per month, starting at $600 billed yearly (2 or more users); Premium: a custom quote, for 5 or more users. Plans include unlimited signature requests, and there is a 30-day free trial. Per Dropbox Sign, the HubSpot integration is available on Essentials, Standard, and Premium.

QuickSigner is the cheap option, placed last here because it takes a build. There is no native HubSpot integration listed on QuickSigner's site; connecting it means a build on its REST API and webhooks.

Prices from quicksigner.com/pricing: 5 documents a month on the Free plan. Business: $5 per user per month, or $48 per user a year; Professional: $15 per user per month, or $144 per user a year. You get unlimited documents on Business and Professional, and signers don't need an account, an app, or a fee. There is a 14-day free trial on paid plans.

If you build the connection, the eSignature API is on Professional: first 50 sign requests free, then $0.30 each, with volume pricing above 500 a month. Do not confuse QuickSigner with the Swedish product QuickSign at quicksign.se. Deeper write-up: QuickSigner.

items: Quotes already in HubSpot, and you have or will buy Revenue Hub: start with the native quote e-sign.
Contracts from contact, company, or deal records, and you want a native app: DocuSign or Dropbox Sign.
Lowest published price, and someone can own an API build: QuickSigner.
Whatever you pick, confirm who signs, what saves back to the record, and who administers it before you roll it out.
